Now she is putting additional questions that do not treat the witness as a hostile witness but is continuing yesterday's cross-examination and is requiring additional information of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, with all due respect, my purpose here is to get the truth from the witness, who swore to tell the truth and nothing but the truth, and that's all I'm trying to achieve. The witness was -- the witness has said to us that he was down in the corridors of the basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: The question is: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the warden of the detention centre, because I had to ask him to have Bonic go out and to have protection for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. Can I ask you to tell me, then, this place that you're referring to as a detention centre, how long does -- as a military person, how long is somebody kept in a detention centre for? For how long?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until proceedings were initiated before the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. And in this particular detention centre, as you call it, how long were these prisoners kept there for?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I actually do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. You had indicated earlier on that they were kept there for transition, it was a transition point. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, listen to this: Look at paragraph 18 and - one, two, three, four - the fifth line. And I read this: "I made sure that he was kept in a separate cell because I was aware that his life was in danger. I know that he was detained at the Barracks for several months." Is that the same thing as saying that this place was a detention centre because it was used as a transition point to be transferred? Is that the same thing?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Well, what do you agree with?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that in the case of Bonic, because I had information to that effect and I gave information in my statement. But about things I do not know, I cannot pass judgement.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: In your capacity of investigating and taking the statements, from the time you were a part of this Military Security Service until you were relieved of your position, Bonic -- is it your evidence to this Court that Bonic was the only prisoner that you had dealt with? You did one statement and Bonic -- and that was Bonic? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only prisoner of war from whom I took a statement was Bonic. And in the premises of the exchange commission, I took statements from other people who would not -- who were not prisoners of war but were in most cases refugees, exiles from Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I am speaking specifically - and I think you know that too - with respect to the Travnik situation, what went on at the Travnik basement. And maybe I can assist you. All I'm asking you is: You went there twice a week. You have told us that. Okay? You took statements. You investigated things. The question is: Was Bonic the only person that you had ever dealt with in that Travnik detention centre?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Residovic, please try to avoid interrupting the Prosecution frequently because she's endeavouring to get to the truth. And as it is a hostile witness, she is entitled to leading questions, which she's not doing but she's trying to clarify things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can avoid interrupting, but pursuant to the Rules of the Tribunal the Prosecutor should rely on what the witness said. The witness never said that he conducted these investigations, and he always said that the only statement he had taken was from Bonic. He has explained several times that he took different kinds of statements in another location. But my learned friend repeats here again that he had confirmed that he conducted investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question that the Prosecution is asking you is a clear one. In the Travnik barracks you took a statement from the minor Bonic. That is something you have confirmed. But the question she's asking, you can answer with a yes or no because it is very simple: In the Travnik barracks, did you take other statements from other detainees in addition to Bonic? It's very simple; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that's quite clear. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Now, a very, very simple and clear one too: When you got to the Travnik barracks - and you call it a detention centre, but if you look in paragraph 18, you refer to it as the cells - you said "I had taken him from the cells to Beba and my office." So I assume that it is also a prison in your mind, because you talk of the cells. When you got to the corridor, as you claim, just tell the Trial Chamber if - I'm not asking you to say what you didn't see - did you see other people other than Bonic in the cells?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness. Again, the question is very clear. I must remind you that you're a witness. You're not being accused of anything. As you have taken the oath to tell us the whole truth, we don't see why a question of this kind can be embarrassing to you. The question is quite simple: When you went down there, did you see Bonic alone, or did you see other persons down there? It's yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did see other persons as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But other detained persons who were not military policemen, who were providing security there. Did you see other detained persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were detainees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, these detainees according to what you were able to see, who were they? Were there soldiers of the ABiH, civilians, people belonging to the HVO, Serbs? Who were they? If you know. If you don't know, you can tell us there were detainees and I can't say anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say anything more. Because I didn't have any information as to who was down there in the detention. There were members of the army from the brigades who had committed certain offences; I know that. I know that there were such cases. As for the others, I can't say, because I didn't see who they were. I know about Bonic; I know he was down there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But in the cells, according to your visual memory, how many people did you see? Five, ten, fifteen, twenty, a hundred? Have you got a figure, an approximate figure to give us? It may have been ten BiH persons. Have you got a figure that you can give us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In passing, as I was able to see the number of cells and the number of beds inside, I don't think there could have been more than ten people. Between five and ten people. In those cells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please continue, Madam Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, yesterday when we were doing the examination-in-chief you indicated to the Trial Chamber that you described the barracks as a detention centre. And I quote your words: "Because the condition for accommodation was such that people were not able to remain there any length of time." But could you elaborate for us what is your idea of "length of time." Because you see, you said Bonic was there for several months, and I really think this ought to be clarified for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those premises were probably made by the JNA to meet the standards of a detention centre for -- that would be used in the case of disciplinary offences by the Yugoslav army in those days. The rooms did not have the amenities for lengthy stays. They were small; there were several people inside. So people serving their sentence could not be held there, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that it was not a proper place -- or rather, it was not sanitary or in any other way proper to keep prisoners down there for months? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And from your international-law experience, as you have told us, would you consider that to be inhumane treatment?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President, but I have to interrupt my learned friend once again, because this is up to Your Honours to judge and not the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It is too complex a question for the witness. He answered your question in line 14. It is not necessary to go beyond that, to ask him for a judgement of the legal nature and his competencies perhaps are not proper to be able to appreciate that. So please continue, Madam Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you. And with all due respect, the question was only asked of the witness because the witness presenting himself as an international-law expert. He said he taught international law to the military people. But be that as it may, I'll continue. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, could you kindly explain to the Trial Chamber during mid-1993, other than ABiH soldiers, HVO soldiers, if you were aware of any other militant body on the streets of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you clarify the question, please. What do you mean "militant body"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber hasn't understood the question. I'm looking at the transcript. I don't understand the question. And if the Chamber doesn't understand, then the witness cannot understand either. So will you please rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Point taken, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, in the town of Travnik in mid-1993, the middle of the year 1993, you had indicated to us yesterday that you had seen members of the ABiH soldiers patrolling the streets, HVO soldiers. And my question is: Did you see any other bodies, any other militant bodies or any other army or anybody representing themselves as an army patrolling the streets of mid-1993?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid this question is no clearer. I don't know what you mean by "militant bodies."

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll --

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Does that -- do you mean persons under arms, armed persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... relating to paragraph 27. Let's go straight to it, because I'm entitled to lead you. So let's go. Do you see paragraph 27 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before Madam Residovic intervenes, the question is linked to paragraph 27. The Prosecution is putting the question with prudence, prudently. What do you have to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wish to say that the Prosecution put an identical question to the witness yesterday: "Did you see any other military bodies?" Or "bodies" again, I see in the transcript. And the witness answered: "They were not members of any organisation." So an identical question was put to the witness yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: With all due respect to my friend, that's just the purpose of this exercise.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Paragraph 27. Could you look at it for us: "Foreign Mujahedin were in Travnik during the war. They were usually armed with AK-47s and wearing uniforms, which were a mixture of three-quarter shorts and camouflage jackets. They usually didn't have badges. I didn't see them come into the barracks when I was there. I don't know where they were based but I used to see them very often on the streets." And I can continue, but I think you can assist us now, can you? Did you see the presence of any other bodies on the streets mid-1993, middle of the year, in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The question is simple: Are you confirming the contents of paragraph 27?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Ibrisimovic. We haven't heard you for a long time, so we're listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have just a correction in paragraph 27 that was explained by the witness. In line 3, he explained today that the word "usually" should be deleted. The witness explained that they didn't have badges, whereas my learned friend put it slightly differently. And perhaps the witness could explain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Witness, you are confirming the contents of paragraph 27 with the reservation of the handwritten corrections that you made during your meeting with the Prosecution, having deleted the word "usually."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And also, specifying that you crossed out the word "Bermuda" and exchanged it for "trousers," and you also underlined a sentence. But the general content is something you are confirming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Benjamin, the time for the break approaches. In fact, we've gone beyond it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think I have a few more question. But if the Court is mindful of taking the break now, I'm in the hands of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As we started at 10.20 again and as we have to stop every hour and a half for technical reasons, we are going to adjourn and we will resume at twenty-five past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Benjamin, you have the floor for your final questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, aside from statements that you may have received from HVO prisoners and the like, did there come a time when you also received reports of another nature with respect to destruction and damage?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive reports or statements from HVO prisoners. I didn't have any access to those statements, nor did I receive any reports about destruction.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. I'll be specific so we can move on. Paragraph 20 of the statement, please: "Salko Beba and I went to Guca Gora in the summer of 1993 after we had received reports that Mujahedin had damaged the monastery." Could you assist us with that, please.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Salko Beba received that information. I was in the premises of the exchange commission. He came to fetch me by car. He told me to take the paint from the office left over from the painting we had done before, and we headed off in the direction of Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So, then, what you said in your statement on the 11th and the 14th of November is not exactly true; is that what you're saying? Because you said you received reports, but now you're saying you didn't receive any report.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say I received reports, but it had been reported, that we had been informed, that this information had reached us. Somebody probably told Mr. Beba by telephone or in some other way. But I did not receive a report in writing or orally from anyone. I didn't have the authority to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. I can only go by what you said in your statement, you'll agree. And so I'll ask you this question so that we could clarify the whole issue of the -- your duties: In your capacity as a Military Security Service personnel, did you at any time receive any reports with respect to beatings of prisoners at the Travnik basement, with respect to looting, with respect to damage to property, whether by Mujahedin or otherwise? Did you receive any reports? Did you ever receive any reports?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. All reports went to Mr. Salko Beba, and I didn't have access to those reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So when you say in paragraph 24 of your statement, "each brigade had a Deputy for Military Security Service who was responsible for investigating disciplinary and criminal offences," where do you get those offences from that you investigate? Who relate about them [sic]? Who made those reports for you to carry out investigations?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was making this statement, the question had to do with the structure of the Military Security Service and their competencies. So each brigade had a deputy commander for military security who was responsible for investigating disciplinary and criminal offences by members of those units.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: That's just my point. So were reports made with respect to the behaviour of the members of the brigade with respect to beating of prisoners, any criminal offences -- were reports made to you?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Earlier on you indicated that you were subordinated to Mr. Salko Beba; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And Mr. Salko Beba was subordinated to Mr. ...? Could you assist us. Who he was subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I was subordinated to Mr. Salko Beba. I assisted him in the operations group. I did not have a post by establishment within the operations group, so I was not subordinated. Mr. Salko Beba was subordinated to the commander of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Did you take instructions from Mr. Salko Beba?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: With respect to dealing with criminal offences, drafting of orders, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In connection with drafting orders, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Did you draft orders in the military on your own accord?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Upon whose instructions did you draft the orders?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Salko Beba.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And Mr. Salko Beba was subordinated to who?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the commander of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there's an error in line 56 -- page 56, Line 21. The witness said, "Yes, in connection with drafting orders." And then he added, "Not in connection with criminal reports." That is what the witness said. The wording here is quite different in the LiveNote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it would be better for the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. witness to tell us. Mr. Eminovic, you told us that you drafted reports following instructions from Mr. Beba. We agree on that, don't we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not reports but orders, pursuant to instructions received from Mr. Beba.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Orders. I see. Very well. Were there occasions when you had in your possession reports regarding destruction drafted by someone else and that you had in your hands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution called your attention to paragraphs 24 and 25. I'm asking you to look at them closely, paragraphs 24 and 25, and they're very precise and they come from what you said. It says that "each Brigade had a Deputy for Military Security who was responsible for investigating disciplinary and criminal offences." And you describe the procedure in paragraph 25. The Chamber is wondering if this person, who is in English designated as deputy for Military Security Service, was that you? Did you have that position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And to the best of your knowledge, who was the person who had those responsibilities in addition to Mr. Beba or as the deputy to Mr. Beba?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As stated here in paragraph 24, those persons were in the brigades and not at the level of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And you, did you have any relationship with those people or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How could you, then, describe their work in such a precise manner? How did you know that the procedure required two signatures and all these things? How did you know all these things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The information comes from the rules of military service, and they're linked to my previous education in the military academy regarding the functioning of various units in the army. In principle, the functioning and organisational structure of the BH army was very similar to the organisational structure of units and military formations in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam Benjamin, do you have other questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Just a few, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Eminovic, I am a bit confused and I think we need to clear it up because you had indicated that you didn't have a rank by name per se but you performed the duties, as you said in paragraph 4 of your statement. And if you look at the second line of paragraph 25, it says that "the Military Security Service investigated it using assistants as required to take statements, reconstruct events, and, if necessary, secure the crime scene." And I'm wondering, were you a part of this?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not. As I said a moment ago, this was linked to the brigade. The operations group did not have the capacities, the capabilities to engage in such activities, because every brigade in those days had an assistant commander for security and at least two security assistants or clerks.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I don't know. Let's just get the order, then. Salko Beba was subordinated to Alagic; am I correct? We said that already. We established that, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good. Let's move on. Now I want to ask you: How were the information -- the reports sent to the corps? How -- explain the chain for me. Could you explain the chain of events, who collects the report, what happens? And maybe if you look at paragraph 7 of your statement it may assist you.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reports from the operations group towards the corps - and I am talking in theory how things should have functioned; in those days communications were very poor. We lacked the technical devices for various information to follow an established procedure - each assistant commander of an operations group, in addition to reporting to the commander of the operations group, was also duty-bound regarding his own responsibilities and within his own terms of reference to inform the command of the 3rd Corps -- or rather, the service in charge of such things.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: So the 3rd Corps was informed, according to your statement in paragraph 7 in the statement. That was the chain. Eventually the 3rd Corps, they reported to the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how the chain went. Now, whether those reports were actually sent out, I don't know, but that was how the chain of command was established and the functioning of military organisations was established in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Would you be able to help us as to whether -- because I'm not sure if you can be of assistance to us, because I don't know what your functions were, but I'm going to ask you still. Was there a district military court functioning in Travnik during the period 1993 and 1994?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the district military court was functioning during that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And as far as you know, based on reports that were received, are you aware whether any 3rd Corps soldiers were investigated or punished for beatings of prisoners in the Travnik barracks?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive reports, but I don't know whether there were any investigations of members of the ABiH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And in your capacity as a member of the Military Security Service, you are not aware of any prisoners - and this is your evidence to this Court now - you were not aware of any prisoners, whether civilians or HVO soldiers or otherwise, who reported beatings?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: You're not aware of that. Okay. And this would be my final question to you: Are you aware that there were lootings and burnings in the Guca Gora area?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that property was being looted of citizens of Croat nationality. I didn't have any reports to that effect. I was not in a position to receive reports of that kind. But I did hear that such incidents were taking place.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: What is confusing me is that is Travnik and the Guca Gora area such a very big area that you yourself couldn't see? Couldn't you tell us what you saw? Didn't you see anything?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Guca Gora is some 10 kilometres away from Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: The conflict was on, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Were you aware of what was going on during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: What was happening around you? Were you aware of what was happening in the environment, what was happening in the surrounding areas? Were you aware?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, five or six citizens of Croat ethnicity abandoned the town of Travnik and across the Vlasic Mountain went to the territory under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska. Most citizens of Croat ethnicity from Travnik had left the town on foot. About 5.000 people left Travnik on foot, and this is at the other end of Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And do you know if they left on their own volition?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that there were conflicts, clashes, shootings, but I also heard that they had left following HVO members who were on the front line against the Army of Republika Srpska and they crossed into territory controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska. Now, the reasons behind this, believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Do you know, then, if there was a lot of conflict going on in the streets of Travnik with respect to the Mujahedins? Were they terrorising people? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was happening in the streets of Travnik linked to the Mujahedin is something I referred to in my statement. They behaved in a hostile way even towards members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina if they saw them drinking. As for any details linked to the activities of the Mujahedin in the streets of Travnik when fighting was going on, I don't know, because there weren't any major battles in Travnik between members of the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Could you tell -- for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, could you - if you know, that is - could you tell us who the Mujahedins may have been subordinated to, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. As far as I know, they were not within the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time. They didn't have insignia on their uniforms, and they behaved in the way I described in paragraph 27 of my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And this is my last question to you: The statement that you gave on the 11th and the 14th, 2003, of November, which is just about four months ago, and the proofing that you did on the 19th of April, 2003 [sic], which is just two days ago, are those clauses that you made in the statement, are they true and correct?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is the end of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Eminovic. Like my learned friend, I will start with the statement that you gave to the investigators of the OTP on the 11th and 14th of November. Is it true that the investigators on that occasion were Mr. Mr. Guenter Schweiger and David Re?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the very beginning, my learned friend asked you how you made that statement, and you answered her question. You noted that you did not receive the statement in our language on time. Tell me, did you ask for that statement to be provided to you in our language?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, because I didn't feel sufficiently qualified to testify in English before the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In our language, the statements was shown to you only two days ago when you came to The Hague; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Eminovic -- or actually, you can confirm that once again - though you told us that yesterday, that you and your colleagues in 1993 were working under extremely difficult conditions which it is hard to imagine from the standpoint of normal living conditions today - is what I am saying true?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the work you did, were you a witness of the fact that this was a year when members of the armed forces and ordinary citizens were engaged in superhuman efforts to simply survive?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, was that a time when, under such difficult conditions, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was actually being formed as an armed force, which in 1993 had to wage a battle on two fronts? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a native of Travnik, as someone who was living in Travnik in those days, can you tell the Trial Chamber that those days the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was engaged in combat activities and defending lines running across several hundred kilometres?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, Mr. Eminovic, you were 21 years old; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the war had interrupted your education.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, you had absolutely no work experience.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answer to His Honour Judge Swart, you said that like everyone else you were obliged to work on an average 12 to 13 hours a day, sometimes 20 hours a day, simply to fulfil your obligations and make a living.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that that year as a member of the Exchange Commission for Prisoners of War you took statements from persons who had been expelled, exchanged, or who had fled from areas and they had been expelled by the JNA and later the HVO. Could you tell us roughly how many statements you took during that year under the conditions as you have just described them?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of that year, I took at least 300 to 400 statements from persons expelled from the area of Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a young man, you had to face the terrible dramas of individuals who were talking about Keraterm, Omarska, and other sites of major crimes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you and your colleagues in the commission were doing was a basis for the beginning of the work of this Tribunal and the many cases that were filed before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to your immense efforts, is it true and were you aware that you lacked the professional and capable personnel for all walks of life in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that even in the army, which was being formed, and in other bodies there was a shortage of qualified personnel who could in an understandable manner for a civilised person write orders, reports, et cetera? Did you encounter problems of that kind?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that reason, Mr. Eminovic, why you assisted one another and specifically Mr. Beba in carrying out those duties?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, the Prosecution in the course of their examination showed you two orders. I would like to ask you to look at the order of the 4th of July once again as well as the one from the 28th of June for me to be able to ask you several questions about it. In view of the conditions under which you were working, were significant errors frequently made in orders issued or any other documents issued by a particular body?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Working on other assignments, were you able to see that there were certain contradictions in those orders?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at this document dated the 28th of June, 1993 and page 2 of that document. It says that "Eminovic Jasenko is a member of the operations group command." And you have explained that you were never a member of the operations group command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown another document which was issued only seven days later, that is, the 4th of July, 1993. And in paragraph 4 of this document, it says that you are an assistant for military security.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If one were to view this, then under normal circumstances you could say that you had been demoted from a member of the command to an ordinary clerk. But as you have testified in court, you were neither of those things. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answer to several questions from the Trial Chamber, you described the work you did. In the order of the 28th of June, it says that you were supposed to control the work of checkpoints. Did you ever control the work of checkpoints in your life?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the second order, I think you already explained to the Trial Chamber that you never carried out the duties listed in that order; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, when Mr. Schweiger and Mr. David Re met you in Sarajevo on the 11th and 14th of November, 2003, as far as I was able to gather from your answers, they showed you these orders, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with these orders and your own position as described there, you told them exactly what you told the Trial Chamber today; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, in none of the paragraphs is it stated that these orders were shown to you nor that you gave additional explanations in connection with those orders; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, even though you were ready to be a witness of the Prosecution and to cooperate fully, at the time you gave your statement what you told representatives of the OTP was not included in that statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Eminovic, you said that this was a period when the army was being formed. So is it true that it was being formed -- that at the same time the operations group Bosnian Krajina was being formed as an entity?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also true that many people then were doing several jobs and there were frequent changes regarding the position of individuals?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to show the witness two documents which the Defence -- will you please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this the time when the operations group Bosanska Krajina was being formed?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown two documents which the Defence found in the archives of the BH army. And I would just like them to be marked for identification because I don't think we can tender them through this witness into evidence. These are two documents. One was June 1993, and the other number is 0940 of 28th of June, 1993 -- 28th of August, 1993 -- 20th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to the question of the learned friends, you said that in mid-1993 Salko Beba became assistant commander of the OG Bosanska Krajina for security matters. This is an order. I don't know whether you have seen it and you can speak about it, but I would like to ask you that for provisional military war duties a person had to be appointed by the 3rd Corps command or the staff of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the bottom of the order there is a sentence saying that "the OG is a formation of provisional character and people appointed on the basis of that order continue -- will continue to carry out their duties"?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Salko Beba in mid-1993 was a member of the State Security, that is, of the police of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that at that time he was president of the Commission for Exchanges of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was the third function that Salko Beba was appointed to.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this one of the ways in which one proceeded at that time; when a person had to carry out several duties, whether he was appointed to them or not, in order to survive?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the other document. 28th is the date. -- 20th of August is the date. From the document, we can see a proposal of the commander of the OG, Mehmed Alagic, asking of the command of the 3rd Corps to have this previous order annulled because at the time the OG did not exist as a formation. Is that what is said in that proposal?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this one of the documents which confirms the full complexity of the conditions under which we had to work when the bodies were just forming and being disformed in a very short period of time?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that document, point 4 - it is in fact the answer to your question - it is clearly asked that Salko Beba should remain permanently employed as State Security inspector in the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina for the Zenica sector and only when he was reappointed on the basis of a new 3rd Corps order it was necessary to resolve this issue so that his service in the MUP could continue to exist.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this one of the documents that in a very concrete way points to the concreteness of the conditions and complexity of the conditions whereby bodies were being formed and people being appointed for permanent or ad hoc tasks?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please mark these documents for identification. And then the Defence will suggest -- propose their adoption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the documents produced by the Prosecution, does the Prosecution ask the documents to be given to them? To have these documents admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think there was an objection on the other side that the witness had not recognised the documents, and so they objected to the fact that it be going in. So I think it would just have to be marked for identification, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Then we will give two provisional numbers. We have several documents coming from the Prosecution. You have the documents of the Prosecution. Can you give us the provisional numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The statement dated -- for the record, Your Honour, the statement dated the 14th of November, 2003 will be Prosecution Exhibit 103, marked for identification, and 103/E, marked for identification. The order dated the 4th of July, 1993 will be Prosecution 104 and Prosecution 104/E for the English translation. The order dated 28th of June, 1993 will be Prosecution Exhibit 105 and Prosecution Exhibit 105/E, all marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have just resolved the question of the Prosecution documents. Now we have the two documents provided by the Defence. We need numbers for them too, provisional numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The document dated the 12th of June, 1993 will be marked DH125 and DH125/E, marked for identification. The document dated the 20th of August, 1993 will be DH126 and DH126/E for the translation, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, I would like, Mr. President, to say that given the fact that the statement of Eminovic has been identified, the one that was presented to him during cross-examination as a hostile witness, it could be only used to disqualify the witness and not as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it has been given a provisional number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, several times you explained to us that you assisted Mr. Salko Beba in conducting some of his duties, and then you explained that you had a military ID of the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, in the broader area of Travnik, from Turbe, Travnik, Guca Gora, all the way up to Zenica, this was the permanent area of battles; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Without permission to move, it was difficult to pass through the area and especially to carry out provisional jobs that you yourself had to carry out for the benefit of Mr. Beba as transport of the military police; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the reason why the security body of the 3rd Corps issued this ID to you, so that you could move around more freely in conducting those limited jobs that you had to perform for Mr. Beba?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, since you mentioned a name in your statement, who issued you with that military ID.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Salko Beba, and he received the ID from the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it an idea which was issued by Ramiz Dugalic as his immediate senior officer?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who issued that. The Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps issued this, but I don't know who signed the document -- the ID.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you had not been appointed to any post in the OG or any other military formation. Is it true that a security body of the 3rd Corps is a body that could appoint a person in a military formation or to a military post [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the fact that you had a military ID, you were quite clear about not belonging to bodies of the 3rd Group or to the OG, is that so?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the translation, there is a mistake. I said, "Is that true that the security body of the 3rd Corps was not able to appoint persons to military duties." In the transcript it says the opposite. So can this be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of yesterday, Judge Swart put several questions to you in relation to the practice and theory of the application of international law. You answered that you had seen how the military police was securing the monastery in Guca Gora and the church in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to the question of my learned friend, you mentioned that thefts had been committed in that area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you with the same amount of certainty or uncertainty that in performing your functions had you heard or known about that a large number of members of the army were criminally charged because they had -- that they were thieving and plundering, looting the Croatian houses?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard that reports had been made, but I had no official information about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know and on the basis of information that you heard from other persons, was this one of the reasons why in response to my questions you said that you believed that the bodies of the army tried to have the Geneva Conventions respected?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In respect of the detention in the barracks in Travnik; several questions were asked in that connection. And in connection with Mr. Bonic I would like to ask the following question: Are you aware that after you had taken the statement from him, with regard to the surroundings of his capture and the killing of the soldier and the severing of the ears, did the competent security body bring charges against Bonic? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the crime department of the military police took a statement again about the other circumstances, and I know that criminal charges had been brought against Mr. Bonic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, do you know that when criminal charges are pressed that it is within the competence of the court to determine or extend detention or custody against a person and then it is the -- and then the Military Security Service has no longer anything to do with the case?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the basis of our laws and on the basis of a decision of an investigation judge that a person could be kept in detention for a period of six months?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a lawyer. I don't know about those details.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Eminovic, that in respect to the persons that have been criminally charged, the control of the prison conditions is carried out by the court instigating the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that security -- the securing of the persons is carried out by the court police, that is, not part of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In response to a question of our learned friend, you said you heard that some of the detainees were mistreated, and in your statement you said that Salko Beba spoke about this to responsible persons in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 17th Krajiska Brigade; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you heard about this mistreatment, is it true that you did not hear who these persons were; that is to say, whether they were arrested members of the army or perhaps persons that were awaiting to be transferred to the prison in Zenica or were awaiting exchange? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that that person of the 17th Krajiska Brigade informed Salko Beba that such excesses were taking place with people coming -- soldiers coming into the barracks and that he hadn't the means or the power to prevent them from doing that?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please clarify the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said in your statement that the military police that were securing the prisoners were not able to prevent people -- soldiers from coming into the cells. The last sentence was that "Beba spoke on the subject with people from the Krajina Brigade." Is that something that you found out about? This is point 5.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the discussion between Salko Beba and people of the 17th Brigade, after that, did you hear about further mistreatment of people who were detained in the Travnik barracks?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In response to Judge Swart's question, you spoke about lecturing on your knowledge about humanitarian law and the Geneva Conventions, and you quoted that besides having knowledge from the academy you had some orders and documents coming from the 3rd Corps. In the cross-examination yesterday I showed you some specific orders relating to protection of buildings, and yesterday in response to the question of the Judge, I asked and was provided from Sarajevo yesterday an order of the 3rd Corps which we found in the archives of the ABiH army during investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I ask this document to be shown to the witness so that I can then subsequently put a question to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, my question is first: Have you seen this document before? And if so, was it part of the literature, if I can call it that, that you used when training military policemen how to perform their duties and how to collect data for war crimes?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this a document that you referred to in answer to a question from His Honour the Judge when you said that you also had some documents from the 3rd Corps command?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in view of the fact that the witness has identified the document as one that he used in his work and which he received from the 3rd Corps command, I should like to tender it into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution opposes tendering this document into evidence. If Your Honours, please, have a look at page 1 of the B/C/S version. It appears from what the document looks like that the lower part of the document is missing. There is no signature on it, and the document looks like - and I'm not suggesting that it actually happened - but it looks like as if certain portions of the first page were not copied. Defence may be in a position to explain what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Defence, for your comments regarding the appearance of the document and the first page of the document in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And if Your Honours and the Defence -- from the Defence side please also consider that the holes in the document - and this is again underlining what the Prosecution is saying - that the holes indicate that a certain portion of the document is missing. And quite interestingly, in the document we used today the signature of the person is at the very bottom of the document. I don't know for what reason portions of this document are missing. Defence may please explain it to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Mr. President, I should like to point out that the witness recognised these documents - these are excerpts from the Criminal Code relating to war crimes - as being documents that he used during the course of his work, and it is on that basis that the document cans be admitted. Secondly, I already said that I asked my investigators in Sarajevo yesterday because I know that one of the Prosecution witnesses whose statement was disclosed to us said that he had compiled this document, and so our investigators took steps and found in the army archives this document. This is a wartime document which, probably because of the conditions during wartime, has many shortcomings. This was sent to me by fax yesterday. It was translated in great haste. And it is quite possible that during the process of copying some technical errors may have been made. But I can bring the original document which arrived with the fax so you can see it, that it arrived from Sarajevo yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the fax line is obviously missing. The fax report is obviously missing on the document that has been provided to the Court and the Defence, and the Court is certainly very well aware that the issue of the signature of the accused Hadzihasanovic has been addressed in the recent filings of the Defence in respect to the admissibility of the Prosecution's documents. So the Prosecution would like to know whether the original of this document has the signature of the accused Hadzihasanovic on it and, if so, we would like to get the original of the document, please. The Prosecution is not objecting against admitting into evidence the legal provisions which are attached to the 26th of June, 1993 order, but it's objecting against the admission into evidence and it's also objecting against marking it for identification. And we're talking about the actual order of the 26th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are two problems: There is first articles from the Penal Code, 141 and onwards, which do not pose any problem at all, and that go as far as Article 155. And a second point, that is the first -- that is, the first page in B/C/S of a document coming from Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic, but on the technical level there's a little problem and that is that the bottom of the page seems to have been cut off because theoretically one should see a little stamp. It must have been marked somewhere. And this is missing. So one might imagine that the document was cut in half and that a bottom of the page has been added without a signature. So perhaps it would be a good idea to have the original at least. So we're going to mark it for identification only, in view of the objections, though most of the document consists of articles from the Criminal Code, which do not cause any problems -- unless Mr. Bourgon has something to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Concerning the admissibility of documents, as the Chamber knows, this is a subject that we will be discussing next week for at least two days, to see whether a document is admissible or not. As underlined by my friend from the Prosecution, for many of the contested documents the question of signature is an important question. For documents that do not have a signature, the Defence notes this fact as a grounds for challenging the admissibility of a document, because a document without a signature does not allow the Chamber to draw conclusions from it without having a sufficient amount of information, without knowing that the document is sufficiently reliable to allow the Chamber to make useful conclusions from it. Therefore, a document of this kind cannot be admissible except through the support of additional evidence in the form of testimony. In this particular case, we have a witness in the chamber. The witness knows not only the instructions he used in training but he also knows that those instructions came from the 3rd Corps and that he used those instructions for the training he gave to military policemen. Therefore, Mr. President, we feel that all the necessary information is available allowing the Chamber to draw the necessary conclusions; that is, an order was given at a higher level, at the level of the court, then transmitted to a lower level, to give everyone - both the OG and the brigades and all members of the army - the need to familiarise themselves with this. And this witness was aware of this document. He took the document and used it in giving instructions to military policemen, as he mentioned during his testimony. For those reasons, Mr. President, we feel that this document has all the necessary characteristics to be admitted into evidence. We are quite ready to have it marked for identification and then to produce the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But before giving you the floor, Mr. Eminovic, the document you have before you consists of two parts: An order, on the first page, without signature, and which can provoke a discussion. However, let me ask you, though it is difficult for you to tell us, do you remember seeing this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are telling us that the first document - that is, the first page - you saw it, the page dated the 26th of June, 1993. Are you giving an affirmative answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's quite astonishing because all the persons in this courtroom when shown a document that they saw ten years ago, I can't see that anybody could be so affirmative about it. But you're telling us that you did see this document and you read this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read this document, and during the training for the military policemen a couple of copies were already in the premises of the military police and they were informed about it, so the document was available to all members of the military police company to read it. That is why I remember it. It was a public document in the sense that every member of the army had to familiarise themselves with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: The question is whether you have read the companion letter, not the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the question of the Judge is: Did you read this first page? And do you remember reading it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't read the first page. The material that I received didn't have this first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, you see? So the document you received did not include this first page; however, the articles on genocide, et cetera, you remember having read them and seen them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, based on this information we just got, we certainly do oppose even marking this document for identification. We certainly do oppose tendering into evidence -- it into evidence, and the Prosecution still would like the Defence to provide the Chamber with the full copy of this document. There are many questions that remain unaddressed by the Defence, even after they were given the opportunity to explain what happened to the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that that is a fair question. I've already told the Trial Chamber what happened. After we received a statement from one of the Prosecution witnesses who is on the list, who claimed in that statement that following instructions of the 3rd Corps commander he had typed out this document, in the archives of the BH army we found the document. I didn't feel it necessary for me to have that document when cross-examining this witness. However, yesterday in answer to a question from Judge Swart the witness said that during training he also used the document which he had been provided by the 3rd Corps command, and that was the reason why yesterday we asked for that document to be provided. I will provide the Trial Chamber tomorrow with the page with the fax report on it. In my office I think I have it. If the Trial Chamber feels that this document should only be marked for identification as the witness cannot recognise the first page of this document, the Defence will try to bring persons to the court who will be able to show the full authenticity of this document for the Trial Chamber. What prompted us to provide this document was yesterday's statement by the witness. So my question to the witness is:

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, even though you didn't see this first page, where this -- the rest of the document came from, the document that you used for training policemen?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Though there were several copies in the premises of the military police, I received a copy from Salko Beba, who said it had come from the 3rd Corps command, and I used this document in the training of military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am now asking for the document to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution has certainly not a problem in respect to the articles which are attached to the cover letter; however, the Prosecution opposes any attempt to even mark the cover letter or the order of the 26th of June, 1993 for identification. The document raises a number of questions which have been addressed and haven't been answered yet. It can only be marked for identification once these questions have been answered by our learned friends from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber will deliberate and render our decision after you have provided us tomorrow at the latest with a cover page and explained the origin of the document, and then we will see whether it can be marked for identification. Unless you already have it; if you have it -- Madam Usher, go and fetch the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My interpreter was probably listening to what I was saying in the hall downstairs in the Defence room, and he sent the document he used for translating, and you can see the fax number of my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution doesn't have a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Usher, show this copy, please, to the Prosecution. It's the same document. Nothing has changed. We just have the fax number of the sender.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's exactly the point, Mr. President, Your Honours. Nothing has changed, and I still wish to know from the Defence what happened to the lower part of this page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber will rule on this problem. I must tell everyone that it is quarter to 2.00 and we should adjourn. How much more time do you need for your questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have just completed my questions for this witness. Thank you, Mr. Eminovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Mr. Dixon, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: We have no questions arising from the cross-examination by the Prosecution. We do note, however, that many of the questions that were put by the Prosecution during their cross-examination were questions that could have been put in examination-in-chief. They were not necessarily questions that were put to challenge the witness. However, the Prosecution has elected to label this witness as a hostile witness, and for that purpose they can no longer, in our submission, rely upon this witness as a witness of truth. It's of course a different matter what the Defence wish to submit about the evidence of the witness and, of course, what Your Honours decide, given all the evidence in the case, what weight to attach to his evidence. But nevertheless, even though, in our submission, a lot of the cross-examination was not true cross-examination, there are no questions arising that we wish to put. One final matter, Your Honour, is that we also wish to note that the objections raised by the Prosecution regarding some of the documents are significant, and this is a matter to be addressed next week, because this is precisely what the Defence has objected to with the Prosecution seeking to introduce some 600 documents as though it was a straightforward matter and that no problems are to arise. However, it is evident that many of these documents do need to be looked at in great detail. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Following the questions of the Defence, does Madam Benjamin wish to take the floor?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And in light --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And do you need --

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: In light of what has transpired in the cross-examination, I'm afraid I just have to have one question with the witness, because it is because of this very statement that was made why this -- why the application was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: At page 68 of the transcript, line 6, my learned friend said to you, "At the time you gave your statement, what you told representatives of the OPT was not included in that statement," and you said "Yes." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please remind him exactly. It went so quickly that the Chamber and witness are rather lost.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Page 68 of the transcript, line 6. My learned friend put to him that "at the time you gave you statement what you told the representatives of the OTP was not included in your statement," and you responded, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I don't know if we can get a copy of the page of the transcript. Can we? Page 68, line 6. It was put to him that what he told the representatives of the OTP was not included in his statement, and he said yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. Good. Now, please, the statement was made on the 11th and the 14th of November, 2003. It was made in English. You answered this morning that you speak English and that you understand English, and you signed the statement in English. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Before the official statement was made, a draft was presented to you for you to make any corrections; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And I'd like to show the witness this document and give it to the Court. If you look at the top of the statement, the first page, you will see "Draft 13.11.03," and it was presented to you for you to make any additions, subtractions, omissions, deletions, whatever. And did you make the necessary corrections?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good. Then the official draft -- the official -- Mr. Eminovic, could you please answer because when you nod, nothing comes up on the thing. So could you please answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you got your final statement and you signed it in English; is that true?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that is when I asked to have the statement in Bosnian, because I didn't feel sufficiently sure of myself to give a statement in English in the Tribunal. You must understand that a mother tongue is a language in which some things can be much more easily explained than I would be able to do in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I am very much aware of that. But we are coming to that. Okay? So you signed the statement on the 14th in English. You got to the Tribunal on the 19th of April, 2003 -- 2004, sorry. I presented the statement to you in B/C/S. Was that correct?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I asked you if you had any omissions, additions, corrections of any sort to make, and you made some corrections like the ones we showed today. Was that correct?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: In the presence of the interpreter and the investigator, I asked you if you wanted me to conduct the proofing in English or if you wanted an interpreter to speak your language with you. You said you wanted it conducted in English; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. During our conversations, on a number of occasions I used the services of the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
