utterances.text: You used the services of the interpreter when you made the corrections on the statement. But I asked you if you wanted me to do the proofing in your language, and you said no, you were comfortable with English. And didn't we do the proofing in English?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: At that time, didn't I give you the opportunity to add, subtract, delete whatever you wanted to that statement? Didn't I give you the opportunity?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there wasn't time for us to do the proofing in 20 minutes. In paragraph 4 of my statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: In 20 minutes? We didn't have a time limit on you to do the proofing, so I don't know where you got 20 minutes from. We started the proofing at 9.30 in the morning and we had all day. On Monday, the 19th of April, 2004; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On Monday, we started at 14.00 hours. The driver picked me up from the hotel, and he returned me at 15.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Correction, we did do it in the afternoon. But we didn't have 20 minutes. We started at 2.00. You're right. We did it Monday afternoon. And we completed it. But did you ask to have any omission -- did you agree -- did you say to us that what was told to the OTP was not in your statement? Did you say that to me?

utterances.speaker: JASENKO EMINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those sentences are underlined in this text.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. Eminovic, I think you can understand English very well. And we're going to go through it slowly. Okay? You said to the -- in answer to my friend that at the time you gave your statement what you told representatives of the OTP was not included in that statement; which means, I take it, that when I showed you the statement on Monday, the 19th what was missing, you were asked to delete, add, subtract, whatever. You did not add anything. So is it true now to come and say that what you told representatives of the OTP was not included in the statement when you had the opportunity to so do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think there may be a lack of understanding here. The witness in answering a question from the learned friend said on several occasions when she showed him two orders, he said that those orders were shown to him in Sarajevo. And he also said that he gave the same explanation as he had given here in court. I just asked him whether that fact was included in the minutes. Actually, I put a leading question to him: Is it true that this fact was not recorded in the minutes? And the witness said yes. Therefore, in my opinion, the minutes or the statement was not complete. But in good faith of a lawyer's ethics, I think that the Prosecutor can confirm that what the witness said is quite correct, and that is that two orders were shown to him in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a very, very serious matter; hence the reason why we took the route we took. Because this very witness, when he was shown the orders - and he can tell you - I showed him the orders at the proofing. And he said to me that he had never seen those orders, he doesn't know the orders, he doesn't know how his name got into there. So I am at a loss, really. Because when you can make a statement that you -- you premise your statement with the fact of his knowledge of English and the fact that he didn't get a B/C/S statement and then you say to him, "Even though you were ready to be a witness of the Prosecution and to cooperate fully, at the time you gave your statement" -- you haven't said anything about orders -- "what you told representatives of the OTP was not included in your statement." And he said, "Yes." Now, if that is what it is, what happened on the 19th of April when the statement was presented to you and you were asked "do you have anything to add, do you have anything to delete,?" You corrected what you had to correct and you didn't add anything further. So how could you come now and make such an allegation and could be allowed to make such an allegation and could be allowed to make such an allegation? I think we need an explanation, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, will you try and answer this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When giving my statement in Sarajevo, representatives of the OTP showed me an order of the 4th of July, 1993. I told representatives of the OTP at the time that my name was on that order; however, that I was absolutely not involved in those activities. I said that here in court yesterday as well. And the question of the Defence was whether any of those documents at the proofing session prior to this trial, I was shown the other order as well [as interpreted]. And I said that I wasn't a member of the operations group but that I was aware of the contents of that order, because I mentioned that order on banning illegal sales of cigarettes in my statement on the 11th and 14th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, the question that we are discussing at present has nothing to do with the witness. The question was raised by the Defence with a very precise aim in mind, and that is to show that when a witness is -- meets with the Prosecution and they have almost a whole day with him, the members of the Prosecution make notes, they draft a statement, and then they show it to the witness, and the witness is asked "Do you agree with what is in it?" The witness says yes, he makes corrections, and the statement is finalised. The only thing that the Defence wanted to take note of was that that statement did not -- that the investigators, when they came to Sarajevo did not include the sentence saying "We showed the witness two documents and he didn't recognise them." So we are saying that ethics of an investigator or a lawyer or a policeman when taking a statement should note everything of importance, and if the witness doesn't recognise two documents, this is something that should have appeared in the statement and it would have saved us a lot of time today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, you will be given the floor. When the investigator saw you in Sarajevo and prepared this written statement, did they -- they showed you an order and you said you didn't recognise that order, even though your name figured on it. When it was -- when you reread it in English, why didn't you ask that your comment on the order should appear in the written statement saying "I wish to indicate that you showed me an order on which my name appears. I formally contest this document, which I never had in my possession?" Through its question the Defence wanted to highlight this, saying that your statement wasn't complete in that sense. So why didn't you request that this point appear in the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't request it because I didn't know. No one asked me whether such details should be included. I am not a lawyer. I am not familiar with the procedure. I didn't know that this statement would be used in the way it has been used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have identified the problem at least. We have to complete this hearing. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, since my learned friend from the Hadzihasanovic Defence somehow tried to touch on the professional ethics of the people who took the statement in November 2003, I wish to inform the Court that the two individuals who took the statement, the two representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor who took the statement certainly complied with all rules and regulations and there's certainly not any reason to believe that they haven't complied with professional ethics. The Prosecution has made inquiries with the two individuals - namely, Mr. Guenter Schweiger and Mr. David Re - whether these two orders have been shown to the witness or not. If the Chamber so wishes, the Prosecution can provide both as witnesses to this court and they may explain to the Court what happened at the time. The inquiries reveal that is Mr. Schweiger can't -- and I have to go back to my e-mail to be absolutely correct -- that he doesn't remember whether these orders were shown to the witness; and Mr. Re, according to the information I got, doesn't remember it either. However, there may have been one of the two orders within the binders which were taken at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the time with them for the interview of the witness, and it cannot be excluded that one of the two orders were shown to the witness. However, if the Court so wishes, the Prosecution can call either of them as witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not a question of ethics, it's a procedure conducted within the investigation. And the Chamber has noted on a number of occasions that when a witness is interviewed by the OTP, the witness prepares a written statement and the documents that are produced are not part of a recapitulating document. So when a witness is interviewed and when certain documents are shown, as happens in civil-law countries, there should be a list of the documents shown and an indication whether the witness confirmed or denied a document. And if there had been such a list, it would indicate that the witness contested such-and-such a document. As that was not the procedure, we have this kind of problem. It's not a problem of ethics but a problem regarding the procedure applied in the investigations. If we wish to avoid such problems, it would be desirable that when a witness is interviewed and if there are documents shown to him the witness should be asked to contest or confirm those documents in writing. And when we come to the oral proceedings in the Tribunal, then those documents could be produced. Madam Benjamin, it was not a question of the ethics of the investigators but a problem which is linked, rather, to the procedure applied much more than an ethical issue. Therefore, if there are no further questions, the Chamber wishes to thank you. You were planned for one day; you have stayed for two days. For a moment I thought you might be kept for a third day but thanks to the wisdom of all the parties and the fact that the Judges have no further questions for you, we wish to thank you and we wish you a safe journey home. And I should liking to ask Madam Usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, we have a witness planned who will have to wait again until tomorrow, so we will resume work tomorrow with that witness; is that right? I hope he was informed about the postponement of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: We have the witness available tomorrow who was scheduled for today, and the witness has been informed accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We will of course rule tomorrow regarding the question of the document. There's another remaining issue, and that is the Prosecution produced a document marked in his own language, in the language of the witness. What does the Prosecution intend to do with this document? It is the B/C/S document which the witness corrected in his own hand. Does the Prosecution request the admission of that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, for identification, please, because I think it goes to the root of what -- the basis of the application that was made in respect to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the document in B/C/S with handwritten notes by the witness is -- the request has been made that it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, what will be the number for this B/C/S document, please, marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P106, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber apologises to the staff, who have had to work for half an hour longer. The hearing is adjourned, and we will all meet again tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of April, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
